spans.s:
jār-á, m. lover;
 paramour, adulterer.

jar-at, pr. pt. (-ī) of √ jṝ, old, frail, 🞄decayed, tumble-down;
 m. old man.
jarat-ikā, f. old woman.

jarat-kāru, m. N. of a Ṛṣi;
 f. 🞄N. of his wife: -priyā, f. id..
jarád-aṣṭi, a. long-lived.

jarad-gava, m. old bull;
 N. of a vulture.

jar-ás, f. aging, old age, decrepitude;
 🞄-as-a, —˚, a. id..

jarā-vat, a. old, aged;
 -sandha, m. 🞄N. of a prince of Magadha and Cedi.
jar-i-tā, (cs. pp.) f. N. of a fabulous 🞄bird: a‿ari, m. N. of Jaritāʼs eldest son (whose 🞄foes are demolished).
jar-i-tṛ́, m. invoker, singer, worshipper.
jar-i-mán, m. old age, decrepitude, 🞄death from old age.

jarjar-ita, pp. become worn out or 🞄decrepit;
 bruised, mangled, lacerated or pierced.
jar-bhur, intv. of √ bhur.
jār-íṇ-ī, a. f. having a paramour.
jārya-ka, m. kind of animal.
